commands.review_summary:
The PR retires durable browser-tab registry rows after 24 hours of repeated unavailable ownership checks, threads a coherent clock through lifecycle cleanup, adds boundary tests, and documents the new cleanup limit.

PR surface: Source +19, Tests +33, Docs +3. Total +55 across 4 files.

Reproducibility: yes. from source, with medium confidence: an unavailable durable close result is deferred without deletion, while the browser session-tab store has a reject-new capacity limit. This review did not execute a live browser reproduction because the checkout is read-only.

target.title: fix(browser): retire durable tab rows whose browser never returns
target.body:
## Problem

Durable session-tab cleanup defers whenever it cannot prove ownership. When `/json/version` fails because the browser is gone, `closeTrackedCdpTarget` returns `{ status: "unavailable", reason: "browser-identity-lookup-failed" }` (`cdp.helpers.ts:330-347`, `:404-412`), and the registry returns without deleting:

```ts
if (outcome.status === "unavailable") {
  params.onWarn?.(`deferred tracked browser tab ${tab.nativeTargetId}: ${outcome.reason}`);
  return 0;
}
```

Nothing else removes a row by age. Every delete path in `session-tab-registry.ts` is guarded by an explicit untrack, an ignorable close error, or a terminal outcome; `trackedAt` is only ever preserved on upsert, never compared against `now`. A `cdpUrl` that comes back on a *different* browser yields `ownership-mismatch` and is retired — but a browser that simply never returns leaves its rows permanent.

The sweep runs by default (`config.ts:271`, `enabled: raw?.enabled ?? true`), which makes this louder rather than self-healing: it re-claims those rows every 5 minutes, fails, and warns forever.

## Why it escalates

`browser.session-tabs` is opened with a hard cap and no TTL (`session-tab-store.ts:38-42`):

```ts
{ namespace: "browser.session-tabs", maxEntries: 5_000, overflowPolicy: "reject-new" }
```

`reject-new` has no eviction fallback — `enforcePostRegisterLimits` returns immediately for that policy (`plugin-state-store.sqlite.ts:432`) and `assertCanInsertPluginStateEntry` throws `PLUGIN_STATE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED` at `:503`. That throw travels `trackOpenedBrowserTab` → `browser-tool-session-tabs.ts:90-108`, whose compensation block closes the tab that was just opened and rethrows.

So once the namespace fills with unreachable rows, every `browser open` on that profile opens a tab, closes it again, and errors — permanently, since nothing reclaims the rows.

The existing suite already pins the capacity behaviour ("fails closed at capacity without evicting an existing ownership record", `session-tab-registry.sqlite.test.ts:594-622`) and pins that `unavailable` survives (`:624-659`). What was never covered is any path *out* of that state.

## Fix

Bound the retry rather than the store. When a close attempt reports `unavailable` **and** the tab has gone unused past the retire window, drop the row instead of deferring again:

```ts
if (now - tab.lastUsedAt >= BROWSER_TAB_UNREACHABLE_RETIRE_MS) {
  params.onWarn?.(`retired unreachable tracked browser tab ${tab.nativeTargetId}: ${outcome.reason}`);
  deleteClaimedTab(tab, params.onWarn);
  return 0;
}
```

Chosen over a namespace `defaultTtlMs` (which `OpenKeyedStoreOptions` does support, `plugin-state-store.types.ts:53`) because a TTL also expires rows for tabs that are alive and reachable, silently giving up cleanup on them. This branch only fires on a cleanup attempt that already failed to prove ownership, so healthy tabs are untouched.

The window is 24h and deliberately generous — a laptop asleep overnight or a browser restart must not drop tracking. A browser that does return after that long almost always carries a fresh `browserInstanceFingerprint`, which retires the row through the `ownership-mismatch` path anyway, so the row's remaining value is close to nil.

Also threads `now` through `closeTrackedBrowserTabsForSessions`, matching `sweepTrackedBrowserTabs`, so lifecycle cleanup can be exercised on a coherent clock.

## Verification

New test asserts both edges — the row survives at `RETIRE_MS - 1` and is gone at `RETIRE_MS`:

```
✓ retires a durable tab whose browser stays unreachable past the retire age
Test Files  3 passed (3)
     Tests  152 passed (152)
```
(`session-tab-registry.sqlite.test.ts`, `extensions/browser/index.test.ts`, `browser-tool.test.ts`)

The new test is load-bearing: neutralising the retire condition to `if (false && ...)` fails it on the terminal assertion, with `["NATIVE-gone"]` still in the store.

`run-tsgo.mjs` clean, max-lines ratchet clean. Four macOS-only failures elsewhere in `extensions/browser/src/browser/` (Info.plist / LaunchServices / `com.microsoft.edgemac`) reproduce identically on a stashed tree, so they are pre-existing on Windows and unrelated.

Note the fixture change in "retries pending lifecycle cleanup even when normal sweeps filter the session": it tracked at `now: 1_000` but called lifecycle cleanup on the wall clock, making the row appear decades idle. Passing `now: 2_000` keeps the test's intent (a pending lifecycle cleanup survives a transient failure) on one clock.

## Follow-up from #110797

This is the second of the two findings I raised on #110797. The first — CDP's `No target with given id found` not matching the ignorable-close list — landed in that PR (`cdp.helpers.ts:463`). This one was flagged by ClawSweeper as a P1 as well and is still open on `main`.
